subject: Performance MAP: reproduce throughput/TTFT gaps and finalize close cadence
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Kickoff: MAP + perf benchmarks (throughput / TTFT)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick follow-up on the perf numbers. We ran a short throughput/TTFT sweep last week and are seeing ~25-40% worse TTFT and a large spike in 95/99 tail at concurrency > 32 compared to the numbers in your public MAP. I attached the raw logs (finapps-bench-logs.csv) — they include sequences, concurrency, and token counts.

We need a short mutual action plan that lays out: the exact reproduction steps, tooling we expect you to use (or that we'll supply), and a target close date — ideally by the end of next week (Jan 25). Our procurement timeline is tight and we need the performance reconciliation to be part of the decision pack.

Two quick notes about our run: it was against your hosted API in us-west with a sequence length mix (8/32/256) across synthetic and recorded traffic. We used Locust as the load driver and a custom tokenizer that differs slightly from GPT tokenizers.

Can you propose a MAP and a repro plan? If you can reproduce with our artifacts that will help reduce friction.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Director of Platform Engineering
FinApps, Inc.

Attachments: finapps-bench-logs.csv (csv)
From: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-01-18T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + perf benchmarks (throughput / TTFT)

Elena —

Appreciate the logs and context. I've put together a targeted MAP and repro plan (attached) that covers:
- Workload shapes: sequence mix (8/32/256), tokenizers, request distributions
- Concurrency sweep plan: [1,4,8,16,32,64] with 10-minute steady windows
- TTFT definition: client-observed first token latency (cold vs warm cache)
- Tooling: we'll run with your Locust artifacts and our internal wrk2 adapter so results are comparable
- Environments: hosted (us-west) and our Dedicated staging pool (identical hardware profile)
- Acceptance criteria: reproduce within ±15% TTFT and no >20% increase in 95th tail at target concurrency

High-level timeline:
- Jan 18–20: align on methodology and exchange artifacts (tokenizer, locust config)
- Jan 20–22: Redwood internal reproduction + cross-tool runs (our wrk2 vs your Locust)
- Jan 22–24: consolidate results, triage any mismatches; prepare a short findings pack
- Jan 25: MAP readout and decision sync (close cadence)

I've linked the HubSpot deal and shared a draft MAP on Drive for comment. Please confirm if the acceptance criteria look right; if so we'll start the reproduction run with your artifacts as step 1.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-FinApps-perf-plan.pdf
Related: https://hubspot.com/deals/FIN-2027-003, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B1-FinApps-MAP
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sarah@finapps.com
Date: 2027-01-19T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + perf benchmarks (throughput / TTFT)

Dylan —

Thanks, that plan looks sensible. A couple of clarifications before you start:
- We'll attach our Locust artifacts and the tokenizer sample (locust-config.yaml, tokenizer-sample.txt). Our tokenization yields ~1.15x tokens on average vs the tokenizer you publish.
- We ran tests against the hosted endpoint (no dedicated pool) and saw the largest divergence at sustained concurrency (32–64).
- We'd also like a short competitive baseline: if you can run a matching workload against CloudX's hosted tier (same model family) so we can compare end-to-end behavior, that would be helpful.

We'll expect a reproduction attempt with our artifacts before you run any cross-tool comparisons.

Meeting availability: Jan 24th 10–11am PST for readout (if that works).

Elena

Attachments: locust-config.yaml, tokenizer-sample.txt
From: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-01-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: FinApps MAP — triage plan and owners

Team —

Quick internal plan to triage the methodology delta from FinApps:
1) Reproduce with FinApps artifacts (Locust + tokenizer) against hosted us-west endpoint (owner: Karthik)
   - Note: run both with warm KV cache and with cold starts, capture TTFT and token-level traces
2) Build tooling adapter for tokenization delta (owner: Neha)
   - Normalize token counts so we can compare per-token latencies
3) Run cross-tool comparison (wrk2 vs Locust) and CloudX baseline (owner: Karthik)
4) Capture traces and per-request metadata, produce a short repro-summary CSV and a trace bundle (owners: Karthik + Neha)
5) Draft findings and next-step recommendations for Jan 25 readout (owner: Dylan)

I've attached a short triage checklist. If we see persistent 95/99 tail behavior at concurrency >32, suspect either client-side queuing or an unexpected scheduling/eviction pattern in the runtime's cache. Karthik — start the reproduction this afternoon and post initial numbers.

—D

Attachments: triage-checklist.md
From: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-01-22T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + perf benchmarks (throughput / TTFT) — interim results

Elena —

Quick update from our reproduction runs (summary attached):
- Using your Locust config + tokenizer we reproduced TTFT differences but narrowed the delta. Published MAP TTFT vs reproduction (seq mix aggregate): 120ms vs 135ms (≈12.5% delta).
- Tail behavior: at concurrency 64 we see elevated 95th: published 280ms vs repro 360ms (≈29% higher). At concurrency 32 the gap is smaller (~18%).
- Cross-tool runs (wrk2 vs Locust) show consistent medians but Locust introduced jitter under high sustained open connections — likely client-side connection pooling settings.
- CloudX baseline (matched config) showed similar median TTFT to published, but CloudX's tail improved with its request shaping; this suggests differing scheduling/backpressure handling.

Attached: repro-summary-20270122.csv, traces.zip (trace bundle, small). Next step: we recommend a focused 30-min call to show traces and agree whether we'll accept new acceptance thresholds or run a mitigation test (adjust request shaping / KV cache sizing).

Proposed sync: Jan 24 10am PST (matches your availability).

Thanks,
Dylan

Attachments: repro-summary-20270122.csv, traces.zip
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sarah@finapps.com
Date: 2027-01-25T15:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + perf benchmarks (throughput / TTFT) — interim results

Dylan —

Thanks for the detailed repro and the trace bundle. The findings align with what we suspected: a mixture of client-side shaping and runtime scheduling differences explains most of the tail delta. We're happy to proceed with a short mitigation window (adjusting request shaping and cache sizing) as part of the MAP.

A couple of administrative notes for the MAP:
- Procurement will accept the performance readout as part of the decision pack. Our target is to issue a PO by Feb 7, provided the final MAP includes a short SLA addendum on tail latency for concurrency targets.
- Please include the small credit ask and the updated acceptance thresholds in the final MAP readout.

I'll hold the Jan 24 slot for a demo/readout if you still want it; if you prefer Jan 25 we can do a follow-up. Either way we are on track to close next week.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director of Platform Engineering
FinApps, Inc.

Attachments: final-terms-redlines.pdf
